neighbours.label: Permission status: whether someone is allowed or permitted to do something under a rule (not be allowed to drive, not permitted to enter, No access rights), vs the same rule-like sentences without permission
fire: Passengers are not allowed to stand while the bus is moving.
Under the new rules, students will not be permitted to use phones in class.
Only members of staff are allowed to enter the storage room.
Dogs are not permitted on the beach between May and September.
Patients will not be allowed to eat anything after midnight before surgery.
Children under twelve are not allowed to swim without an adult present.
During the exam, candidates are not permitted to leave the hall.
Visitors without a badge will not be allowed past the front desk.
quiet: Passengers usually read or sleep while the bus is moving.
Under the new rules, students will learn coding in their first year.
Only members of staff know where the storage room key is kept.
Dogs love running on the beach between May and September.
Patients will feel hungry after midnight before surgery.
Children under twelve learn to swim at the local pool.
During the exam, candidates write their answers in blue ink.
Visitors without a badge often get lost on the way to the front desk.

predictions: ' allowed'/' permitted'/' be' in a rule about what a person may do reach 0.4-0.7; the same contexts stating an obligation-free fact or 'allowed me to' as enabling stay under 0.2.
notes: Card: peaks on ' allowed' x8 (you will not be allowed to drive), 'No' (No creation rights), '准' (获准进入), '||No restrictions'. Probe: not be allowed to drive 0.640, not permitted to take photographs 0.597, to be allowed into backstage 0.533, PermissionError('No ...') 0.356, smoking permitted? 0.307; 'feel tired' 0.031, 'the grant allowed me to buy' 0.156 (enabling sense, weaker).
